assumptions: `grid_unit` is a gcd OF OBSERVED rows; the brief lists it under MEASURED, so MEASURED wins and it is skipped (documented in the constant GRID_IS_MEASURED rather than left as an unexplained overlap).

The brief's MEASURED list omits keys the real file actually carries (ci_arm, ci_note, grid_unit_meaning, resolved_block_size, resolved_block_size_source, endpoint_seen, headline_arm, note_grid, engine_version, rows_sha256, unc_naive_history, prompt_tokens_sum-style derived stats). With only the brief's set, --strict would fail against the REAL file on those keys; so each was classified: launch/measurement notes -> MEASURED; engine_version and rows_sha256 -> DERIVED (engine_version is argv-independent but IS a function of the launch artefact the builder reads, and rows_sha256 is the integrity link between the compared argv and the rows it was derived from). unc_naive_history -> DERIVED (pure function of rows).
Added --config <path> so red tests perturb a /tmp copy while --check still builds from the repo artefacts; the real disk file was never written.
next_unit_hint: Any future setup field must be added to DERIVED or MEASURED in tools/best_config_build.py or --strict will (correctly) turn red; tests/test_best_config_check.py::test_key_sets_are_disjoint_and_cover_disk_config enforces coverage without --strict.
